brief: Goldman's IG credit desk reports IG cash outperformed a choppier macro week because positioning into well anticipated supply was the overpowering technical. Issuance of $73bn, the third busiest week of a record year, was in line with the $70bn estimate, but composition mattered more: 46 deals in four days, no jumbos beyond a $6.5bn GSK trade, only 7% of supply in the long end against 20% over three months. That mix drove curve flattening, the IG 30y basket 2bps tighter versus 0.5bp for 5y and 10y. The desk calls $50bn next week and, absent a surprise MSFT deal whose odds it sees as higher, does not see supply driving credit underperformance. Prime data: IG long short ratio at a 2 year low, corporate bond ETF shorts up 14%, equity net exposure in the 6th percentile. The AI basket had its best week versus IG100 in over a year on supply shifting away from the subsector and AI momentum. CPI printed above expectations, roughly 90% odds of a hike are priced and GIR now calls 25bp Wednesday. Given yields, the technical set up and cheap vol, the desk argues credit is not the best short for the next four weeks.
